description:
Privacy requests get no deadline and no audit trail: due_on is never set, no PrivacyAuditEvent is written, a future received_at is accepted and the request type can be switched silently (MEDIUM)

What happened (2026-10-22 09:44 UTC, MCP as team07):
- PrivacyRequest.create {party_id: <team07 test party>, request_type: "export", received_at: "2026-10-22"}
  → 9ec61249, status "received", due_on null. due_on is in _readonly_fields (server-owned), and is
  still null on every later read. Same on Suryodaya (9d78bb92).
- received_at "2020-01-01" (150815a7) → accepted, due_on null; nothing marks it years overdue.
- received_at "2027-06-01" → accepted on create (29274ccc) and on update (9ec61249).
- PrivacyRequest.update request_type "export" → "erasure" on 9ec61249 → accepted.
- PrivacyAuditEvent.list → 0 rows on both instances after all of the above, although its kind
  enum includes "received".
Refused correctly: nonexistent or other-tenant party, other-tenant company_id, 2026-02-30.

Expected: a privacy request carries its statutory deadline from receipt (due_on, e.g. 30/45
days), cannot be received in the future, and every receipt and change of type is recorded in
the append-only PrivacyAuditEvent log.

Impact: data-subject requests can be logged with no deadline, so nothing can flag them as
overdue; the audit log that should prove when a request arrived and what it asked for is
empty; an export request can become an erasure (or the reverse) with no record; a backdated
or future receipt date moves the deadline. Agents reading these records get no due date to
act on.

Reproduce: PrivacyRequest.create on any party you can read; PrivacyRequest.get → due_on null;
PrivacyAuditEvent.list → no "received" event. Update received_at to a future date → accepted.

Scope checked: MCP create/update/get/list, both instances. REST and any UI fulfilment flow not
tested (status/outcome are read-only to this seat; no transition tool is exposed).
